introduced.event_name: NCC 1983 — planned ERA² and Logix Athena premiere
introduced.timeline_note: Planned premiere on the opening day of NCC, 16–19 May 1983; not a confirmed shipment date.

specification.status: Accepted planning baseline; production and electrical qualification pending.
specification.register_compatibility: Preserve documented ERAv1 R0–R15/CPSR, instruction semantics, data formats and calling conventions.
specification.execution_improvements: Short in-order interlocked pipeline, ALU result forwarding, explicit load-use stalls, early branch-target calculation and flushing; preserve ERAv1 PC and instruction semantics, with no new visible delay slots.
specification.external_cache_policy: Interface support target only; no external cache included in the Athena base BOM until selected. DMA coherency must be specified.

tlb.refill_policy: Prefer software-managed refill initially; concurrent instruction/data translation remains an implementation decision.

specification.faults: Precisely defined restartable faults for demand paging. ERAv1 already has Data Abort and Prefetch Abort; ERA² strengthens the restart contract rather than introducing aborts for the first time.
specification.floating_point: Optional external FPU interface; no integrated or bundled FPU promised.
specification.performance_target: Measure workload-specific improvement over 8 MHz ERAv1; former 2–3× objective is not a general promise. Report clock, cache, memory and software configuration with results.
specification.compatibility: Documented ERAv1 user binaries retain an execution path. New privileged/MMU features require OS support; no socket, mainboard or unqualified peripheral compatibility implied.
open_design_items: Board memory timing and qualified speed bins
ROM electrical timing and patch/cache synchronization
Detailed fault continuation and late bus-error behavior
pipeline_contract: False conditional instructions have no architectural/data-memory side effects or associated data faults.
Younger wrong-path instructions cannot commit registers or memory.
Interrupts enter at documented restartable boundaries, including multiply and multi-access instructions.
Instruction timings and forwarding paths require implementation-level verification.
fault_contract: Earlier instructions completed; later instructions have no architectural effects.
Faulting instruction has no changes or documented resumable state; report instruction address, access address/type and cause.
Validate translations/permissions for multi-access instructions before effects, or define explicit continuation state; device accesses must not be blindly replayed.
Post-acceptance external bus errors are distinct from recoverable translation/protection faults; no claim that all external effects are undoable.

instruction_cache_design.candidate: Direct-mapped physically tagged cache with 16-byte lines; organization remains subject to layout and traces.
instruction_cache_design.refill: Coordinate four-word prefetch with requested-word-first refill and early restart where feasible; cancel obsolete branch fetches and prioritize demand data.
instruction_cache_design.decision_gate: Compare compiler, Abacus, interpreter and kernel traces within the 142000-transistor planning envelope.

memory_interface.handshake: Programmable READY/wait controller, independent refresh and bounded DMA ownership.
memory_interface.dram_target: Qualify 120 ns row access / about 240 ns random cycle; 150 ns fallback with about 270–300 ns random cycle. Geometry alone does not establish timing.

controller_target_12mhz.basis: Engineering budget, not measured; accepted physical request to data, excluding translation, contention, refresh and conflicting open row. Two-clock page transfer requires separate margin qualification.

memory_interface.banks: No two-bank interleaving credit for one-bank base Athena; independently qualify populated server banks.
memory_interface.rom: Cacheable directly executable OS ROM with separate wait-state profile; ROM timing is not assumed equal to DRAM.
memory_interface.clock_scaling: 16 MHz requires recalculated waits; DRAM nanoseconds do not scale with CPU clock.

coherence_contract: Define instruction visibility after loading/modifying code, remapping, RAM patch overlays and DMA-written executable memory.
Uncached device regions and explicit DMA synchronization.
First optional external data/unified cache candidate: write-through, no-write-allocate; policy must be qualified before use.

conditions: Required ordering and draining before relevant DMA/device operations
